guideTitle: 6 Best Lightweight Carpet Cleaners Under $150 in 2026
metaDescription: Compact uprights and portable spot cleaners compared on brush design, drying help, tank clarity and reach, for small rooms, stairs and pet messes.
introParagraphs: Raising the ceiling on a lightweight carpet cleaner is the point where you can stop thinking only about spot cleaning. At this level you can choose a compact upright that covers a bedroom or a hallway in a few passes, rather than treating each stain with a handheld tool.

This comparison mixes three lightweight uprights from Bissell and Hoover with three portable machines, so you can decide whether you need floor coverage or reach. We evaluated listing details and common buyer feedback patterns, and we point out where a spec is missing instead of guessing.

The main tradeoff is simple. Uprights clean larger areas faster but take more storage, while portables fit a closet and reach stairs but demand more refills. The sections below tie each pick to the job it does best.

products.name: BISSELL TurboClean Upright Carpet Cleaner 3952
products.description:
The TurboClean is the most floor-focused machine here, an upright with a 4-row DeepReach PowerBrush designed to work into traffic lanes that a vacuum leaves behind. The maker positions it for everyday and pet messes on carpets and area rugs in small spaces, and says it outcleans a competitive lightweight cleaner, though that claim comes from the company, not from independent measurement. It works with OXY formulas for tougher stains.

The four brush rows are the real feature, since agitation lifts what suction alone leaves. The tradeoff is that the OXY formula is a separate purchase, so factor that in. An upright also needs a bit more storage than the portables in this lineup, and it is not the tool for stairs.

Next to the Hoover PowerDash Pet at a more basic feature set, the TurboClean leans on the brush and the Bissell name. It lacks the Hoover's HeatForce drying feature, which the listing for the Hoover emphasizes. Choose it when you want proven brand support and a wide brush for hallways, bedrooms and area rugs.
products.bestFor: Small apartments and bedrooms that need an upright with a strong brush.

products.name: Hoover PowerDash Pet+ Compact Carpet Cleaner
products.description:
The PowerDash Pet+ is the upgraded Hoover in this group, a compact upright with HeatForce technology to speed drying and an antimicrobial PowerSpin pet brush roll. The listing also notes a larger tank than the base PowerDash, which helps you clean more floor between fills. It supports above-floor cleaning as well, so one machine can take on stairs and upholstery as well as rooms.

The versatility is why it leads this group. You get floor cleaning, spot work and a drying aid in one body, which is rare at this class. The tradeoff is that switching attachments between surfaces adds steps, and it sits at the top of the Hoover family within this comparison.

Against the base Hoover PowerDash Pet, the Pet+ adds above-floor capability and tank volume. Against the TurboClean, it trades the four-row brush for heated drying help. If you want a single machine that handles carpets, stairs and pets in a small home, this is the most flexible option.

products.name: Hoover PowerDash Pet Compact Carpet Cleaner
products.description:
The base PowerDash Pet is a compact upright built around pet messes, with an antimicrobial PowerSpin brush roll and HeatForce drying technology. The listing says it suits pet stains, high-traffic areas, area rugs and small spaces, and recommends pairing it with a Hoover cleaning solution. It is a lightweight design that stores easily.

It keeps things basic. There is no above-floor attachment included, so it is a floor-first machine. For owners who just need hallway and bedroom coverage, that simplicity means less to learn and less to store.

Compared with the PowerDash Pet+, it drops the above-floor option and the larger tank. Compared with the TurboClean, it adds heated drying support but offers less documented brush detail. It is the sensible pick when floor cleaning is the whole job, and when you would rather not pay for features you will not use.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner 4075
products.description:
The Little Green is a portable spray-and-vacuum cleaner with a HydroRinse self-cleaning tool and a 4-inch tough stain tool. The listing notes it cleans carpet, upholstery, car interiors and pet beds, and makes a point of removing dander, dust and pollen from spills. It is not a steam cleaner, and that matters if you expect heat.

It earns a place as the compact companion to an upright. Where the upright handles the floor, the Little Green handles a sofa cushion, a stair or a car seat without hauling out the big machine. The main limits are tank size, which means frequent refills, and the lack of published suction data.

On this list it is the best-known portable and the most compact. Next to the Rosewill with its 49 oz and 53.6 oz tanks, it holds far less water, and next to the Uwant at 18 kPa it publishes no suction number. Pair it with an upright if you want complete coverage.

products.name: Rosewill 550W Portable Carpet and Upholstery Cleaner
products.description:
The Rosewill is a portable machine with a 550W motor, 17 kPa suction and a dual tank layout of 49 oz clean and 53.6 oz dirty. That large capacity is the headline, and it lets you clean a staircase or a couch without constant refilling. The listing positions it for carpets, upholstery, stairs and furniture.

It is the heaviest and bulkiest portable here when full. That is the tradeoff for volume, and you should plan to empty the dirty tank before carrying it. Suction at 17 kPa is a hair below the Uwant, but the larger tanks mean you can keep going longer between stops.

Comparing it with the Hoover PowerDash Pet+, the Rosewill is a spot-and-stair tool rather than a floor machine, and it has more tank volume than the Little Green. If you already own an upright, the Rosewill is the strongest portable partner for upholstery and steps. If you do not, the Hoover is easier to use across a room.
products.bestFor: Stairs, sofas and furniture where tank capacity matters more than size.

products.name: Uwant 18Kpa Portable Carpet Cleaner with Pet Pro
products.description:
The Uwant is a portable machine with an 18 kPa suction rating, a bundled Pet Pro solution, three brush heads and a set of tools. It sprays, scrubs and sucks in one pass and is aimed at furniture, car interiors, pet beds and mattresses. The maker's claim of better cleaning efficiency with its own solution is a company figure, not an independent measurement.

The bundle gives you a ready start. You do not need to hunt for a compatible solution, and the three heads let you change texture. The tradeoffs are unclear tank sizes on the listing and the temptation to overuse solution, which leaves residue.

For a buyer who wants the strongest suction number in this group without the bulk of an upright, the Uwant is the answer. It publishes a higher figure than the Rosewill at 17 kPa, but less capacity data than the Rosewill's clear tank volumes. The Hoover and Bissell uprights are better for floors, and the Uwant is better for everything else.

buyingCriteria.explanation: An upright covers floors faster and uses a brush roll across a wider path, while a portable fits stairs, sofas and cars. If you mostly clean hallways and bedrooms, choose an upright. If you mostly handle stairs and furniture, choose a portable. The Hoover PowerDash Pet and BISSELL TurboClean are uprights, and the Rosewill, Uwant and Little Green are portables.

Suction pulls water out, but a brush loosens the dirt in the first place. Multi-row brushes and antimicrobial pet rolls help with ground-in dirt and hair. The TurboClean uses a 4-row DeepReach PowerBrush, and both Hoover models use a PowerSpin pet brush roll. Portables rely on hand-held brush heads instead.

Carpet that stays wet for hours can pick up odor and attract dirt. Heated drying features and strong suction both shorten the wait. The Hoover PowerDash Pet and Pet+ list HeatForce, and the portables rely on suction alone, with the Uwant at 18 kPa and Rosewill at 17 kPa. Plan for good ventilation either way, and avoid overwetting by making a slow final suction pass in each strip.

Tank volume decides how many refills a job takes, and a listing that does not state it leaves a gap. For a staircase, you want tanks near 40 oz or larger. The Rosewill states 49 oz and 53.6 oz, while the Uwant and Hoover listings do not give sizes.

Some machines include a solution, some work only with specific formulas, and some leave you to choose. Using the wrong product can cause foam or reduce results. The Uwant bundles Pet Pro, the TurboClean pairs with OXY formulas bought separately, and the Hoover listings recommend a Hoover solution.

A machine you cannot lift easily or store out of the way will stay in the closet. Uprights need more floor space, while portables need only a shelf. The Little Green is the most compact, the Rosewill is heavy when its tanks are full, and the Hoover models are advertised as lightweight uprights.

howWeEvaluated.title: Floor coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how well each machine suits full-room work, looking at brush design and body type. The BISSELL TurboClean leads with its 4-row brush, followed by the two Hoover PowerDash models with antimicrobial pet rolls. Portables were scored on spot and stair work instead.

howWeEvaluated.title: Suction and extraction
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted published suction figures and flagged missing ones. The Uwant leads at 18 kPa, the Rosewill follows at 17 kPa, and the Little Green and uprights do not publish a figure. Extraction affects drying time and residue, so published numbers earned credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Versatility
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at above-floor use, tool sets and brush heads. The Hoover PowerDash Pet+ supports above-floor cleaning, the Uwant includes three brush heads, and the Little Green includes a stain tool. The base PowerDash Pet and the TurboClean are floor-first machines.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed storage footprint, tank handling and solution requirements. Portables fit in a closet but need refills, while uprights stay ready but need floor space. The TurboClean and Hoover models give brand support, and the Rosewill gives the biggest tanks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The TurboClean is the brush pick, the Pet+ is the versatile pick, the base PowerDash Pet is the simple pick, the Little Green is the portable brand pick, the Rosewill is the capacity pick and the Uwant is the suction pick.

faq.q: Should I buy the TurboClean or a Hoover PowerDash?
faq.a: The TurboClean offers a 4-row DeepReach brush and OXY formula compatibility, while the PowerDash models offer HeatForce drying support and an antimicrobial pet brush roll. If agitation is your priority, take the TurboClean. If drying and pet hair matter more, take a PowerDash.

faq.q: What does the Pet+ add over the base Hoover?
faq.a: The Pet+ adds above-floor cleaning and a larger tank compared with the base PowerDash Pet. That makes it more flexible for stairs and furniture. If you only clean floors, the base model is enough.

faq.q: Are portable machines strong enough for stairs?
faq.a: Yes, they are designed for stairs, sofas and car seats. The Rosewill's large tanks help on a full flight, and the Uwant's 18 kPa helps pull moisture out. Expect to refill more often than with an upright.

faq.q: Do I need to buy a special solution?
faq.a: It depends on the machine. The Uwant ships with Pet Pro, the TurboClean works with OXY formulas bought separately, and the Hoover listings suggest pairing with a Hoover solution. Using a mismatched product can cause foam or residue.

faq.q: How long will my carpet stay wet?
faq.a: Drying depends on how much water the machine leaves behind. HeatForce on the Hoover models is designed to speed drying, and strong suction on portables helps too. Ventilate the room and keep foot traffic off until the carpet is dry.

faq.q: Is the Little Green a replacement for an upright?
faq.a: No. It is a spot cleaner that sprays and vacuums but has a small tank. It works well beside an upright, handling couches, stairs and car seats. It is not designed to clean entire rooms, and trying to do so means many refills and a lot of extra time. Treat it as the precision tool in a two-machine setup.

faq.q: How should I maintain these machines?
faq.a: Empty and rinse the dirty tank after each use, wipe the nozzle and clean hair from brush rolls. Let tanks air dry with the lid open to avoid odors. On uprights, check the brush roll regularly for tangles, since wrapped hair slows the bristles and cuts agitation. Run a little clean water through the spray path now and then so mineral residue does not clog the nozzle, and keep the power cord loosely coiled rather than tight.
